stages.title: MASTER VOCABULARY: WHAT EXACTLY ARE WE STUDYING?
stages.terms: Structure → process → surface: lithology, bedding, joints, faults and tectonic setting create a template; weathering, rivers, glaciers, waves and human use modify it.
stages.mechanism: A rock aggregate is therefore not “a mineral”, and a landform cannot be inferred from a rock name alone.
stages.consequence: Structure → process → surface: lithology, bedding, joints, faults and tectonic setting create a template; weathering, rivers, glaciers, waves and human use modify it.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: a rock aggregate is therefore not “a mineral”.
stages.answer: Geological structure is the age, composition and architecture of rocks and tectonic features beneath a region, while physiography is their broad surface expression and geomorphology explains the processes that reshape it.

stages.title: CRUST AND LITHOSPHERE: RELATED, NOT IDENTICAL
stages.terms: Moho means the crust–mantle seismic boundary; its wave evidence belongs to Topic 01 and is only cross-linked here.
stages.mechanism: Asthenosphere means the weaker, slowly deforming upper-mantle zone beneath the lithosphere; plates move as coherent lithospheric units over it.
stages.consequence: Crust is compositional; lithosphere is mechanical and includes the crust plus rigid uppermost mantle.
stages.trap: They are useful mnemonics, not complete modern compositional layers.
stages.answer: The crust is Earth’s outer compositional shell, whereas the lithosphere is the stronger mechanical layer comprising the crust plus the rigid uppermost mantle.

stages.title: THE COMPLETE ROCK CYCLE: A NETWORK, NOT A CONVEYOR BELT
stages.terms: Lithification means turning loose sediment into rock through compaction and cementation.
stages.mechanism: Lithification means turning loose sediment into rock through compaction and cementation.
stages.consequence: “Igneous → sedimentary → metamorphic” is one teaching path, not the only path.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: metamorphism normally occurs without complete melting.
stages.answer: The rock cycle is an open network in which melting, crystallisation, weathering, lithification, metamorphism and uplift can connect any rock family through multiple pathways rather than one fixed sequence.

stages.title: IGNEOUS ROCKS: COOLING HISTORY, COMPOSITION AND TEXTURE
stages.terms: Porphyritic means large crystals embedded in a finer groundmass, showing two-stage cooling.
stages.mechanism: Porphyritic means large crystals embedded in a finer groundmass, showing two-stage cooling.
stages.consequence: It does not mean every igneous exposure is oldest or economically primary.
stages.trap: India anchor: Deccan basalt is extrusive flood basalt; Peninsular granites and gneisses have different histories and should not be merged with the Deccan province.
stages.answer: “Primary rock” is an older genetic phrase for igneous rock because crystallisation creates the original mineral framework.

stages.title: SEDIMENTARY ROCKS: SEDIMENT PATHWAY AND FIELD CLUES
stages.terms: Conglomerate has rounded gravel clasts; sandstone is sand-sized; shale is fine mud-rich rock.
stages.mechanism: Conglomerate has rounded gravel clasts; sandstone is sand-sized; shale is fine mud-rich rock.
stages.consequence: Limestone has several origins; do not call every limestone exclusively organic or chemical.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: fossils, ripple marks, mud cracks and cross-bedding can reveal environment, current direction, drying or...
stages.answer: They are sediments/deposits unless lithification into rock is demonstrated.

stages.title: METAMORPHIC ROCKS: PROTOLITH, GRADE AND FABRIC
stages.terms: Metamorphic grade means intensity of temperature–pressure conditions.
stages.mechanism: Metamorphic grade means intensity of temperature–pressure conditions.
stages.consequence: Exam-safe paths: shale/mudstone → slate → phyllite → schist → gneiss is a common increasing-grade teaching sequence, not a universal compulsory path.
stages.trap: Graphite may form from carbon-rich material, but “coal → graphite” is not a universal one-step rule.
stages.answer: Protolith means the parent rock before metamorphism.

stages.title: ROCK PROPERTIES AND APPLIED GEOGRAPHY
stages.terms: Crystalline igneous and metamorphic rocks commonly have low primary pore space but can store groundwater in weathered zones, joints and fractures.
stages.mechanism: Crystalline igneous and metamorphic rocks commonly have low primary pore space but can store groundwater in weathered zones, joints and fractures.
stages.consequence: Basalt aquifers are heterogeneous: vesicular tops and flow contacts may transmit water; compact interiors may not.
stages.trap: A dam, tunnel or foundation requires site investigation; “granite is strong” or “limestone is weak” is not an engineering conclusion.
stages.answer: Rock name alone never determines land use: porosity, permeability, fractures, weathering, structure and site conditions jointly control groundwater, soils, foundations, dams and slope behaviour.

stages.title: CONTINENTAL DRIFT: WEGENER’S EVIDENCE AND LIMITATION
stages.terms: Technically, Continental Drift: Wegener’S Evidence And Limitation is analysed by relating Continental Drift to Wegener’S Evidence, then testing the relationship through Limitation and Pangaea.
stages.mechanism: It must later be distinguished from India’s Gondwana Supergroup of rocks.
stages.consequence: His evidence was powerful, but proposed driving forces were inadequate.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: gondwana here means a southern palaeocontinent.
stages.answer: Continental drift became persuasive because shelf-edge fit, matching rock belts, fossils, palaeoclimate and palaeomagnetism independently point to former continental connections, even though Wegener lacked an adequate mechanism.

stages.title: SEA-FLOOR SPREADING: OCEANIC EVIDENCE AND MASS BALANCE
stages.terms: Ocean floor is geologically young relative to continental shields because it is recycled.
stages.mechanism: Ocean floor is geologically young relative to continental shields because it is recycled.
stages.consequence: The Earth does not expand; ridge creation is balanced by trench destruction.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: magnetic reversals create matching stripe patterns on both ridge flanks.
stages.answer: Sea-floor spreading creates young oceanic crust at mid-ocean ridges, records symmetrical magnetic stripes and balances creation by consuming older lithosphere at trenches, so the Earth does not expand.

stages.title: PLATE TECTONICS: BOUNDARY MATRIX AND LANDFORM DIAGNOSIS
stages.terms: Plate-interior activity occurs at inherited faults, rifts, hot spots and intraplate stress concentrations; boundaries explain global clustering, not every event.
stages.mechanism: Plate-interior activity occurs at inherited faults, rifts, hot spots and intraplate stress concentrations; boundaries explain global clustering, not every event.
stages.consequence: Andes and Himalaya are both mountains but arise from different convergence types.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: plate boundaries are diagnosed by motion and products.
stages.answer: Plate boundaries are diagnosed by motion and products: divergence creates crust, subduction destroys oceanic crust, continent collision thickens crust, and transform motion conserves crust while generating shallow earthquakes.

stages.title: OCEAN-BASIN EVOLUTION: WILSON-CYCLE ANALOGY
stages.terms: The Wilson cycle is an analogy for rifting, ocean opening, subduction, closure and suturing, not a fixed destiny that every ocean basin must complete.
stages.mechanism: A basin can stall, reorganise or avoid the ideal sequence; the examples are analogies, not timestamps.
stages.consequence: Passive margins can accumulate thick sediment wedges and host offshore petroleum systems.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: a basin can stall, reorganise or avoid the ideal sequence.
stages.answer: The Wilson cycle is an analogy for rifting, ocean opening, subduction, closure and suturing, not a fixed destiny that every ocean basin must complete.

stages.title: ISOSTASY AND OROGENY
stages.terms: Orogeny means mountain building through convergence, folding, thrusting, metamorphism, crustal thickening and uplift.
stages.mechanism: Orogeny means mountain building through convergence, folding, thrusting, metamorphism, crustal thickening and uplift.
stages.consequence: Erosion removes mass, exposes deeper rocks and can produce isostatic response; high relief is therefore dynamic, not a one-time construction.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: isostasy means buoyant vertical equilibrium between crust/lithosphere and denser material beneath.
stages.answer: Isostasy explains vertical crustal adjustment, while orogeny explains mountain building through shortening, thickening and uplift; erosion and unloading can then trigger further isostatic response.

stages.title: WORLD-TO-INDIA TRANSITION: STRUCTURE EXPRESSED AS RELIEF
stages.terms: At the highest school-geography scale, India’s six broad physiographic divisions are the Himalaya/Northern Mountains, Northern Plain, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains and Islands.
stages.mechanism: At the highest school-geography scale, India’s six broad physiographic divisions are the Himalaya/Northern Mountains, Northern Plain, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains and Islands.
stages.consequence: They are used here only as structural expressions, not as substitutes for the later detailed physiography owners.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: structure controls broad relief and resource opportunity.
stages.answer: Structure controls broad relief and resource opportunity, while climate, weathering, rivers and human use modify it.

stages.title: SCOPE: GEOLOGICAL STRUCTURE VERSUS PHYSIOGRAPHY AND GEOMORPHOLOGY
stages.terms: Technically, Scope: Geological Structure Versus Physiography And Geomorphology is analysed by relating Scope to Geological Structure Versus Physiography, then testing the relationship through Geomorphology and Cross-link.
stages.mechanism: This package supplies their geological mechanism and clearly identifies those cross-links.
stages.consequence: Exam method: identify the hidden structure, name a region, explain the mechanism, state a surface/resource/hazard consequence, then qualify the relationship.
stages.trap: Therefore geology explains pattern and constraint, not every present landform by itself.
stages.answer: India’s geological skeleton consists of an ancient Peninsular shield, an active Himalayan fold-thrust belt and a sediment-filled Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra foreland basin linked by collision, flexure, erosion and deposition.

stages.title: GEOLOGICAL TIME, EVIDENCE AND DATING CAUTIONS
stages.terms: Numerical boundaries and formation ages are revised as dating improves.
stages.mechanism: Relative dating uses superposition, cross-cutting relations, unconformities, fossils and correlation.
stages.consequence: Fossils are especially useful in sedimentary correlations, but many ancient Indian crystalline and Proterozoic successions are unfossiliferous or sparsely fossiliferous.
stages.trap: Stratigraphy is not merely a rock-name list.
stages.answer: A safe geological chronology combines superposition, cross-cutting relations, unconformities, fossils, radiometric event ages, palaeomagnetism and geophysics; relative order is often safer than memorised numerical ages.

stages.title: INDIAN PLATE: GONDWANA ORIGIN, BREAK-UP, DRIFT AND COLLISION
stages.terms: India is both an ancient continental fragment and part of an active plate system: this explains the contrast between old shield rocks and young Himalayan tectonic architecture.
stages.mechanism: Rifting separated blocks, oceanic crust formed between them, and the Indian plate moved northward before colliding progressively with Eurasia.
stages.consequence: Collision was not a single instant across the whole margin.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: india is both an ancient continental fragment and part of an active plate system.
stages.answer: The Indian plate journey links Gondwana rifting, northward motion, Tethyan ocean closure and prolonged India-Eurasia collision to Himalayan uplift, foreland subsidence and continuing seismicity.

stages.title: CRATONS, SHIELDS AND THE STABILISED PENINSULAR BLOCK
stages.terms: Peninsular India is a mosaic of ancient cratonic nuclei and intervening mobile belts, later cut by faults, rifts and dykes and locally covered by younger sediments and basalt.
stages.mechanism: Peninsular India is a mosaic of ancient cratonic nuclei and intervening mobile belts, later cut by faults, rifts and dykes and locally covered by younger sediments and basalt.
stages.consequence: Metallic-mineral provinces are strongly associated with ancient shield geology, but ore localisation requires specific magmatic, hydrothermal, sedimentary or metamorphic processes.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: commonly recognised shield blocks include Dharwar in the south, Bastar in central India, Singhbhum...
stages.answer: Peninsular India is a mosaic of cratons and mobile belts later cut by faults, rifts, dykes and basins and partly covered by younger sediments and lava, so stable never means uniform, flat or earthquake-free.

stages.title: ARCHAEAN AND DHARWAR SYSTEMS: DISTRIBUTION AND TERMINOLOGY CONTROL
stages.terms: Mains use: In a classification answer, give lithology, structure, distribution, significance and a terminology caution.
stages.mechanism: Mains use: In a classification answer, give lithology, structure, distribution, significance and a terminology caution.
stages.consequence: Do not repeat old claims that all Archaean rocks are entirely unfossiliferous or that one textbook's age span is definitive.
stages.trap: Named examples such as Kolar or Singhbhum are location anchors, not universal rules for every Dharwar rock.
stages.answer: Archaean granitoid-gneiss basement and Dharwar-type supracrustal belts form distinct parts of the ancient shield, and their ore associations reflect specific magmatic, sedimentary, metamorphic and hydrothermal histories rather than age alone.

stages.title: PROTEROZOIC PURANA BASINS: CUDDAPAH AND VINDHYAN
stages.terms: Cuddapah and Vindhyan are major Proterozoic sedimentary basin successions resting unconformably on older basement.
stages.mechanism: Cuddapah and Vindhyan are major Proterozoic sedimentary basin successions resting unconformably on older basement.
stages.consequence: Resource links must be bounded: a whole system is not uniformly mineralised, and Panna diamonds do not make every Vindhyan sandstone diamond-bearing.
stages.trap: Older textbooks group them under Purana, but their detailed ages and correlations are convention-sensitive.
stages.answer: Purana is an older Indian label for Proterozoic basin successions such as Cuddapah and Vindhyan, which rest unconformably on older basement and record long-lived sedimentation rather than one uniform mineral province.

stages.title: GONDWANA SUPERGROUP: RIFT BASINS, COAL AND CONTINENTAL SEDIMENTATION
stages.terms: Coal linkage is mechanistic: vegetation accumulation in suitable low-oxygen settings, burial during basin subsidence, compaction and coalification, followed by preservation from erosion.
stages.mechanism: Lower parts of the succession include glacially influenced deposits in some basins, followed by coal-bearing sandstone-shale cycles and younger continental strata.
stages.consequence: Coal presence is not automatic in every Gondwana unit or every rift.
stages.trap: Gondwana coalfields are not simply surface strips along modern rivers.
stages.answer: The Gondwana Supergroup is a fault-basin continental sedimentary succession with important coal measures; it must not be confused with Gondwana, the southern palaeocontinent.

stages.title: MARINE SEDIMENTARY BASINS, COASTS AND OFFSHORE PETROLEUM LOGIC
stages.terms: Offshore occurrence is therefore geological, not simply because an area is under the sea.
stages.mechanism: Mains use: Explain offshore concentration through basin evolution, not a memorised field list.
stages.consequence: Offshore occurrence is therefore geological, not simply because an area is under the sea.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: coastal and offshore sedimentary basins include Cambay, Mumbai Offshore, Assam-Arakan, Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery and other...
stages.answer: Do not claim every named basin is equally productive or that all offshore oil is young.

stages.title: DECCAN TRAP: FLOOD-BASALT PROVINCE AND BOUNDED SURFACE LINKAGES
stages.terms: The Deccan Trap is a vast flood-basalt province built by repeated, mainly fissure-fed lava flows around the end-Cretaceous to earliest Cenozoic transition.
stages.mechanism: The Deccan Trap is a vast flood-basalt province built by repeated, mainly fissure-fed lava flows around the end-Cretaceous to earliest Cenozoic transition.
stages.consequence: Deccan Trap is a volcanic province, not a soil type.
stages.trap: Black soil linkage is strong but not monocausal.
stages.answer: The Deccan Trap is a Late Cretaceous flood-basalt province of stacked fissure-fed flows whose contacts, fractures, vesicular zones and weathering create step relief, black-soil parent material and highly variable aquifers.

stages.title: HIMALAYA: FROM GEOSYNCLINAL LANGUAGE TO MODERN PLATE TECTONICS
stages.terms: The Himalaya is a continent-collision fold-thrust orogen containing sedimentary, metamorphic and crystalline belts; unlike the Andes, it is not primarily a volcanic subduction arc.
stages.mechanism: Modern plate tectonics explains the driving mechanism through subduction of oceanic domains, collision, shortening, thrusting, metamorphism and uplift.
stages.consequence: Mains use: Contrast the historical geosynclinal description with the modern plate-tectonic mechanism; then draw a labelled cross-section.
stages.trap: The Himalaya is not one simple fold.
stages.answer: The Himalaya is a continent-collision fold-thrust orogen containing sedimentary, metamorphic and crystalline belts; unlike the Andes, it is not primarily a volcanic subduction arc.

stages.title: INDO-GANGA-BRAHMAPUTRA FORELAND BASIN AND ALLUVIAL FILL
stages.terms: Technically, Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Foreland Basin And Alluvial Fill is analysed by relating Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Foreland Basin to Alluvial Fill, then testing the relationship through Cross-link and Flexural subsidence.
stages.mechanism: Correct: It is a sediment-filled foreland basin.
stages.consequence: Thick unconsolidated sediment explains level relief, fertile alluvial soils, major aquifers and dense settlement, but also flood, erosion, subsidence and liquefaction sensitivity.
stages.trap: The plain is not one uniform layer or one age.
stages.answer: The Indo-Ganga-Brahmaputra Plain is not structureless alluvium but a flexural foreland basin whose thick sediment supports fertile soils and aquifers while also influencing floods, subsidence and seismic site response.

stages.title: COASTS, OFFSHORE BASINS AND ISLAND-ARC VERSUS CORAL-ISLAND DISTINCTION
stages.terms: Western India includes the Cambay rift and faulted margin sectors; parts of the west coast show submergent features.
stages.mechanism: The emergent islands are coral, unlike the tectonic island-arc setting of Andaman-Nicobar.
stages.consequence: The island chain also includes sedimentary and uplifted components; it is not simply a row of volcanic cones.
stages.trap: Do not miss this limiting distinction: western India includes the Cambay rift and faulted margin sectors.
stages.answer: Andaman-Nicobar belongs to an active subduction-related arc-forearc system, whereas Lakshadweep consists of coral atolls on a submarine volcanic-ridge foundation; Indian island geology is therefore not uniform.

stages.title: MAJOR LINEAMENTS, FAULTS AND RIFTS
stages.terms: A lineament mapped from imagery is not automatically a proven active fault.
stages.mechanism: Mains use: Use one map plus one mechanism paragraph; avoid asserting current activity without evidence.
stages.consequence: A lineament mapped from imagery is not automatically a proven active fault.
stages.trap: Lineament does not automatically mean active fault.
stages.answer: A rift is an extensional crustal zone, a graben is a down-dropped fault block, and a lineament is a mapped linear feature that is not automatically an active fault.

stages.title: STRUCTURAL CONTROL OF RELIEF, DRAINAGE, GROUNDWATER AND WATERFALLS
stages.terms: In hard-rock terrain groundwater is concentrated in weathered zones, fractures and contacts.
stages.mechanism: Hard-rock groundwater depends on secondary openings.
stages.consequence: Correct: Lithologic contrast, rejuvenation and lava contacts are alternative controls.
stages.trap: Structure guides but does not fully fix drainage.
stages.answer: Geological structure becomes examinable when it explains why relief, rivers, groundwater and resource patterns are spatially organised.

stages.title: GEOLOGY, MINERALS, COAL AND PETROLEUM: ASSOCIATION WITHOUT DETERMINISM
stages.terms: Coal follows basin history; petroleum follows petroleum-system completeness.
stages.mechanism: India's resource map reflects ancient shield mineralisation, Gondwana coal basins, sedimentary petroleum systems, coastal placers and weathering-derived ores.
stages.consequence: It does not imply that all critical minerals lie in one geological province.
stages.trap: NCMM is a current policy anchor, not a geological classification.
stages.answer: Shield belts, Gondwana basins and sedimentary margins are associated respectively with many metallic ores, coal and petroleum, but exploration, grade, preservation, technology, economics and environmental limits decide usable resources.

stages.title: SEISMICITY: HIMALAYA, KACHCHH AND PENINSULAR INTRAPLATE EVENTS
stages.terms: Andaman-Nicobar seismicity is linked to the Sunda-Andaman subduction system and includes tsunami-generating megathrust potential.
stages.mechanism: India's seismicity reflects active plate-boundary deformation in the Himalaya and north-east, subduction near Andaman-Nicobar, and intraplate reactivation in Kachchh and parts of the Peninsula.
stages.consequence: Kachchh is an intraplate high-hazard region with inherited rift faults and damaging historical earthquakes, including the 2001 Bhuj event.
stages.trap: Mains use: Explain source, path/site effect and vulnerability separately; do not equate tectonic activity with disaster magnitude.
stages.answer: India’s seismicity reflects active Himalayan and Andaman plate boundaries plus reactivation of inherited structures such as Kachchh and selected Peninsular faults; seismic zoning is a design generalisation, not earthquake prediction.
